changes.after: City of Collinsville
changes.reason: A May 28, 2026 Troy Times Tribune article, written about a neighboring city's own moratorium, states as an established fact that Collinsville 'approved' a year-long data center moratorium, which is inconsistent with the 'proposed, not enacted' qualifier carried since the 2026-04-29 pass.

changes.before: Recommendation only; not enacted. Planning Commission recommended a 12-month moratorium on 2025-12-11; Collinsville Legistar shows no City Council moratorium matter since that date and the Planning Commission moved on to a text-amendment discussion (matter 5501-2025) on 2026-03-12.
changes.after: Reported as enacted: a May 28, 2026 Troy Times Tribune article states, in the course of describing Troy's own six-month moratorium, that 'Collinsville approved a year-long moratorium.' This indicates the City Council acted on the Planning Commission's December 11, 2025 recommendation at some point before late May 2026. Collinsville's own website (collinsvilleil.org) and Legistar system (both the public site and the webapi.legistar.com/v1/collinsvilleil endpoint) returned bot-protection errors (HTTP 403) or a client-configuration error to every automated retrieval attempt this session, so the ordinance number and exact adoption date could not be independently confirmed.
changes.reason: Direct, contemporaneous confirmation was not obtainable from Collinsville's own records this pass, but a dated news article from a neighboring jurisdiction's coverage treats Collinsville's enactment as settled fact, which is more current information than the 2026-04-29 'not enacted' finding.

changes.before: City Council never enacted the proposed moratorium; per Collinsville Legistar (2026-04-29) the Planning Commission instead took up matter 5501-2025 "Discussion - Data Center Text Amendment" on 2026-03-12, signaling a shift to direct text-amendment drafting in lieu of a moratorium pause.
changes.after: Per a May 28, 2026 Troy Times Tribune comparative reference, Collinsville did in fact enact its proposed year-long data center moratorium at some point between the Planning Commission's December 11, 2025 recommendation and late May 2026, despite the Planning Commission's parallel March 2026 discussion of a text amendment. Ordinance number and exact date not independently confirmed this pass.
changes.reason: See current_status change.

changes.after: active
changes.reason: This reverses the 2026-04-29 finding that the moratorium was 'not enacted' -- but confidence is capped at moderate because the only supporting source is a comparative aside in coverage of a neighboring city's ordinance, not a dedicated Collinsville article, minutes, or ordinance text. A follow-up pass should obtain the actual Collinsville ordinance number, adoption date, and final text directly from city records or a dedicated news source before this is treated as fully confirmed.

changes.before: Extended by Ordinance 17-2025 per City of La Grange ordinance index. Final extension term and current expiration not confirmed in captured records [VERIFY: signed Ordinance 17-2025 text and current expiration/replacement date not retrieved as of 2026-04-29].
changes.after: Ordinance 17-2025 extended the moratorium by 150 days, approved unanimously at the City Council's meeting reported November 10, 2025 (the prior moratorium had expired October 30, 2025 per the ordinance). That places the extension's own computed term at roughly early-to-mid April 2026. The City of La Grange's official ordinance index (lagrangeky.gov/ordinances, checked 2026-07-31 and current through ordinances dated late June 2026) lists 2026 ordinances 01, 02, 05, 07, and 09 through 13 -- covering code-enforcement duties, a zoning map amendment, sign regulations, an annexation, and FY2026-27 budgets -- with no ordinance addressing data centers, a further moratorium extension, or permanent data-center zoning regulations. No City Council action on data centers has been identified since Ordinance 17-2025.
changes.reason: Direct check of the city's own current ordinance index shows no data-center item among all 2026 ordinances captured on the page, and the November 2025 news coverage establishes the extension's own term already expired months before this pass without further action.

changes.after: expired
changes.reason: La Grange and Oldham County appear to share a single Planning & Zoning Commission process feeding recommendations to both the city council and the fiscal court (see the companion ky-oldham-county-fiscal-court-2025 decision in this pass). That joint process only reached a second reading of permanent zoning text amendments (KOC 26-920-5) on 2026-07-21 at the county level -- months after La Grange's own 150-day extension would have run out. This suggests a genuine several-month regulatory gap in La Grange specifically, though it is also possible the city took some informal or unrecorded step to keep the pause in place that this pass could not locate. Recommend a follow-up pass to obtain the signed Ordinance 17-2025 text (try requesting it from the city clerk directly, since the CDN link is blocked to automated tools) and to check whether La Grange intends to adopt whatever text amendment Oldham County finalizes.

changes.after: Still in effect as of 2026-07-31. The Oldham County Planning & Zoning Commission voted unanimously on 2026-06-23 to forward revised zoning text amendments to the Fiscal Court. The Fiscal Court held a first reading of the resulting ordinance (KOC 26-920-5, 'zoning text amendments of the comprehensive zoning ordinance') at a special meeting on 2026-06-29, per the Court's own posted agenda. A closed session on pending/proposed litigation was held 2026-07-14 (subject not specified on the public agenda). A second reading of KOC 26-920-5 was calendared for the Fiscal Court's 2026-07-21 meeting per the Court's own posted agenda. As of this research date, no signed minutes confirming the outcome of that July 21 second reading had been posted publicly, so whether KOC 26-920-5 has been finally adopted -- which would likely supersede the moratorium -- remains unconfirmed.
changes.reason: Direct review of the Fiscal Court's own posted meeting agendas (a primary source) shows the underlying permanent-ordinance process advancing to second reading 10 days before this research date, considerably more current than the March 2026 news reporting the prior pass relied on.

changes.before: Rejected on 2026-04-06 by a 3-5 vote after amendment
changes.after: The moratorium proposal remains rejected (council vote 5-3 against, per Herald Guide coverage dated the meeting as Monday, April 6/reported April 7, 2026). The Parish Council subsequently adopted a permanent data-center zoning ordinance at its June 1, 2026 meeting, unanimously per Herald Guide, establishing the parish's first data-center-specific zoning standards: data centers are permitted in M-1 and M-2 industrial districts, subject to a 300-foot buffer from residential districts, schools, day cares, nursing homes, assisted-living facilities and parks; a 25-foot landscape buffer where adjacent to those uses; a 55 dBA noise cap at sensitive edges; and on-site primary energy generation reserved for the M-2 district. No moratorium was ever in force, but the permanent ordinance directly addresses the regulatory gap that motivated the moratorium proposal.
changes.reason: Herald Guide's follow-up reporting on the rejected moratorium confirmed a replacement zoning ordinance (introduced by Parish President Matthew Jewell) was already scheduled for council consideration on May 18, 2026, and a later Herald Guide article confirms that ordinance's unanimous adoption on June 1, 2026.

changes.after: Moratorium proposal failed (5-3 against, per Herald Guide). Parish President Matthew Jewell's follow-up data-center zoning ordinance was introduced and scheduled for the May 18, 2026 council meeting, and the Parish Council unanimously adopted the resulting zoning regulations at its June 1, 2026 meeting, per Herald Guide -- making St. Charles Parish the first parish in southeast Louisiana with dedicated data-center zoning rules, addressing the same underlying siting/design/operations concerns the moratorium had been intended to pause development for.
changes.reason: Confirms the specific follow-through from rejection to permanent regulation, closing out the future-event VERIFY marker.

changes.after: Superseded. The Montour County Board of Commissioners enacted Ordinance No. 1-2026 ('Data Center Land Use Ordinance') on April 14, 2026 -- before the moratorium's own nominal 2026-05-17 expiration -- amending the County Zoning Ordinance to permit Data Centers as a Conditional Use in the Industrial Zoning District, subject to detailed siting, setback/buffer-yard, noise, lighting, and 'Sensitive Receptor' protections and a Conditional Use review process. changes.after: replaced
changes.reason: This is the best-sourced finding in this pass: the actual signed ordinance was retrieved directly from the county's own website and its enactment date was confirmed by direct visual review of the handwritten signature block (the scanned PDF has no OCR text layer). Ordinance No. 1-2026 does not ban data centers; it establishes a Conditional Use pathway in the Industrial Zoning District with detailed siting, buffer, noise, lighting, and 'Sensitive Receptor' (schools, health facilities, residences, etc.) standards, height allowances reportedly increased from 45 to 80 feet during drafting, and a Conditional Use review/decision process modeled on the county's existing zoning hearing procedures. The original moratorium (Resolution R-11-19-2025) is superseded and no longer the operative instrument for data center siting in Montour County.
